content.title: About
content.content: Tangerine is a small sweet citrus fruit (Citrus reticulata) native to Southeast Asia. It has a bright orange peel, juicy flesh, and a distinctive aroma. Tangerines are usually eaten fresh but are also used in juices, desserts, and various culinary dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tangerines belong to the same family as oranges, lemons, and limes.
There are more than 150 tangerine varieties, differing in size, taste, and peel color.
The name “tangerine” comes from the Chinese Ming dynasty, during which the fruit was first exported to Europe.
The peel is rich in essential oils that are used in aromatherapy and perfumery.
In Chinese culture, tangerines are a symbol of luck and prosperity, especially during the New Year.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Tangerines are an excellent source of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids in tangerines have antioxidant properties that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in tangerines promotes regular bowel movements and helps prevent constipation.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal blood pressure.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: Tangerines are relatively low in calories, making them a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tangerines, including skin rash, swelling, or breathing difficulties.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The natural fructose may be a concern for people with diabetes; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tangerines are typically eaten fresh by cutting them in half and pulling apart the segments. They can be added to salads, yogurts, cereals, baked goods, or used as an ingredient in juices and smoothies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store tangerines in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, where they stay fresh for 2‑3 weeks. At room temperature they lose aroma quickly and become softer.
